title: observability: token-level + KV cache metrics, tracing, dashboards and alert tuning
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: provide token-level visibility for both generation cost/latency and KV cache effectiveness, and consolidate tracing/metrics into a single dashboard with tuned alerts. This PR implements new Prometheus metrics and traces for token/kv events, adds Grafana dashboards that show per-route token cost and KV hit/miss heatmaps, and updates alert thresholds after running workload-driven calibration. Goals: 1) surface token-level cost and latency breakdowns (model, kv-cache, network) to help teams diagnose high-cost requests; 2) expose KV cache hit/miss metrics and per-model cache utilization so serving/runtime can optimize batching and prefetch policies; 3) add tracing spans for KV lookup and cache fills to correlate latency spikes with KV behavior; 4) tune alerts to reduce noise while catching regression in cost/latency. Includes: checklist: - [x] Add Prometheus metrics: redwood_tokens_generated_total, redwood_token_latency_seconds_bucket, redwood_kv_cache_hits_total, redwood_kv_cache_misses_total, redwood_kv_cache_fill_duration_seconds - [x] Add OpenTelemetry spans around KV lookup/fill and serving path, with baggage to include route_id and model_version - [x] Add Grafana dashboards: Token cost/latency overview, KV cache heatmap by model/route, Traces linked to token latency percentiles - [x] Create alert rules: token-cost-per-minute > calibrated threshold, kv_miss_rate > 1% sustained for 5m, token_latency_p90 increase > 50% vs baseline - [x] Add migration notes and a lightweight backfill script for daily aggregates - [x] Run e2e smoke tests + performance canary and tune thresholds based on canary run Result: dashboards are added under observability/dashboards/token-kv, alerts updated in observability/alerts/token-kv-alerts.yml, tracing integrated with sampled traces for production by default at 0.1% sampling. Related: Linear ENG-2345 (observability token metrics), ENG-2411 (kv cache telemetry). Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2345/token-level-observability and Grafana preview screenshots in the PR pipeline. Notes: Prometheus metric names are stable; they are annotated in observability/metrics.md for downstream exporters. This PR intentionally leaves the export to the cost-aggregation job as a follow-up (ENG-2468) to avoid long-running migrations in the same change.

review_comments: Ben Thompson: Nice work. Two asks: (1) split the heavy histograms into separate buckets per model family to avoid cardinality explosion; (2) add a make target to validate dashboard JSONs.
Aisha Patel: Addressed both requests. Moved model_family label into exemplar histograms only and added scripts/ci/validate_dashboards.sh. See commit d4e5f6a.
Miguel Alvarez: Alert thresholds look reasonable after canary but add a note about how we derived the baseline and a quick rollback/playbook.
Aisha Patel: Added alerting playbook to observability/alerts/PLAYBOOK_TOKEN_KV.md and included derivation steps in the PR description.
Sana Rao: Can we sample traces at 0.1% by default and 1% for canary only? Concerned about trace storage costs.
Aisha Patel: Implemented sampling control via config flag telemetry.trace_sampling.default_percent and added deployment note. Canary overriding handled by canary job config.
ci_checks: canary-run: passed (saw expected kv_miss rate drop on prewarm)
release_notes: Added token-level and KV cache observability: new metrics, traces, dashboards, and tuned alerts. Operational playbook for alert response and rollback included.
notes: This change is backwards-compatible. Metric names are additive; no runtime opt-in required. Follow-up ENG-2468 will add aggregated cost exports and ingestion into the cost-analytics pipeline.
